record.paper_title: Progress and open questions in the physics of neutrino cross sections at intermediate energies
record.original_question: In the very low energy-transfer region q0 ≲ 50 MeV, is a local relativistic Fermi-gas description of quasielastic neutrino scattering adequate, or must one instead use more realistic nuclear-structure descriptions such as continuum random-phase approximation or shell-model methods to obtain reliable integrated and differential cross sections?

evidence.quote: Another point of concern is the validity of the RlFG description in the kinematic region of q0 . 50 MeV...

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider quasielastic charged-current neutrino-nucleus scattering on a medium or heavy nuclear target (e.g., $^{12}$C, $^{16}$O, $^{40}$Ar) at intermediate incident neutrino energies. Restrict attention to the kinematic region of very low energy transfer, $q_0 \lesssim 50$ MeV, where collective nuclear excitations, Pauli blocking, low-lying discrete states, and long-range correlations may play a significant role.

Two classes of nuclear models are considered for computing the inclusive integrated and differential (in lepton kinematics) cross sections in this region:

(a) A local relativistic Fermi-gas (RlFG) model, in which the nucleus is treated as a non-interacting relativistic Fermi gas with a local Fermi momentum $k_F(\mathbf{r})$ determined by the local nuclear density, and the nuclear response is built from on-shell single-nucleon knockout subject to Pauli blocking;

(b) Microscopic nuclear-structure approaches such as the continuum random-phase approximation (CRPA), which sums ring diagrams of particle–hole excitations including the continuum, or large-basis shell-model calculations that incorporate discrete bound excitations, residual interactions, and collective modes.

Determine whether the local relativistic Fermi-gas description (a) is quantitatively adequate for computing reliable integrated and differential quasielastic neutrino cross sections in the regime $q_0 \lesssim 50$ MeV, or whether one must instead employ approach (b) (CRPA, shell-model, or comparable microscopic methods) to obtain trustworthy predictions. Quantify the discrepancy between the two classes of models and identify the kinematic and observable conditions under which the RlFG fails.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent CRPA-based calculations have shown that for very forward lepton scattering, low-energy nuclear excitations with ω < 50 MeV contribute nearly 50% of the flux-folded quasielastic cross section, and this strength is not captured by Fermi-gas-based approaches. This indicates the local relativistic Fermi gas is quantitatively inadequate in the q0 ≲ 50 MeV regime and microscopic approaches (CRPA, shell model) are needed there. However, a fully unified, experimentally validated treatment across all relevant nuclei and kinematics remains an active area of research.

status_evidence.title: Asymmetric Relativistic Fermi Gas model for quasielastic lepton-nucleus scattering
status_evidence.snippet: An asymmetric relativistic Fermi gas model for electroweak nuclear response in the quasielastic region, with numerical results for neutral and charged current processes.
status_evidence.claim: RFG-type models continue to be developed and used as baseline descriptions of quasielastic neutrino-nucleus scattering.

status_evidence.title: CRPA low-energy strength in quasielastic neutrino scattering
status_evidence.snippet: At very forward muon scattering, low-energy CRPA nuclear excitations (ω < 50 MeV) account for nearly 50% of the flux-folded cross section; this extra low-energy strength is not accessed in a Fermi-gas based approach.
status_evidence.claim: Microscopic CRPA calculations show that the Fermi-gas description misses a large fraction of the cross section at q0 ≲ 50 MeV, supporting the need for CRPA/shell-model treatments.
